# v2.88-dev

Security hardening release, following a review of the areas that have grown
since the last one — the update/deploy layer, the session lifecycle, and the
routes added over the past few months. One change is user-visible (password
changes now end your other sessions); the rest is defensive work under the hood.

Following this project's convention for security fixes, the notes below say what
changed and what it means for you, without the technical detail of what was
wrong. **Updating promptly is recommended.**

## What's new

- **Changing your password now signs you out everywhere else.** The browser you
  make the change in stays signed in; every other session on that account is
  ended the next time it does anything. If you change your password because you
  think someone else has it, that now ends their session too, instead of leaving
  it valid until it happens to time out.

- **An admin password reset does the same for the account being reset.**
  **Admin → Users → Reset Password** now evicts every session that user has
  open. That is usually the point of the reset, and previously it did not
  happen.

  Both are documented in the in-app help (**My Account** and **User
  Management**) and the README.

## Fixed

- **The page shown at the end of connecting a cloud storage provider** (Google
  Drive, Box, OneDrive) has been rebuilt. It no longer repeats text supplied by
  the provider — you get a clear fixed message and the provider's own wording
  goes to the server log, where it is more use for diagnosis anyway — and it now
  confirms you are signed in as an Admin before it will render at all.

- **Two gaps in how requests are checked for permission have been closed**, one
  on a catalogue route and one in the shared request filter. Neither is known to
  have exposed anything on a normal installation; both are fixed, and the
  affected route now carries the same check every comparable route already had.

## Hardened

- **The update process no longer treats its own configuration as executable.**
  It reads the values it needs from `.env` from a fixed list of expected keys,
  rather than running the file. The same principle is now applied throughout the
  update scripts: version numbers, release names and tokens are passed around as
  data, never assembled into commands. If you keep anything unusual in `.env`,
  note that only the keys the updater actually needs are read; everything else
  is ignored rather than interpreted.

- **Tighter file ownership for the scheduled-job logs.** `/var/log/training-tracker`
  and the log files in it are now owned by root, with the application account
  writing through the group — matching how the update status and log files
  already worked. The update helper also gets a private temporary directory.
  This is applied automatically on update; no action needed.

- **A missing service account is now a hard error, not a silent fall-back.** The
  update scripts drop privileges before running `npm install` and the build. If
  the unprivileged account was missing they used to carry on regardless, without
  saying so. They now stop and tell you to run `deploy/install.sh`.

- **Stricter session-token validation**, and the same minimum-length rule for
  `JWT_SECRET` is now applied everywhere rather than in most places.

## Upgrading

This release adds one database column and applies automatically — no manual
step. Sessions that are already open keep working; they are only affected once
that account's password is next changed.
